coordinates: pixels in the full scan above, origin top left
method: Same conventions as bird-pigeon-pl755.json, mirrored because this pigeon faces right. Each lateral frame cropped at 1.5-1.6x with a 25 px grid and raised contrast; points picked by eye, drawn back onto the crops and corrected. head = eye; shoulder = where the near wing's leading edge leaves the body; wingTip = most distal primary of the near wing; tailTip = point of the tail farthest from the head. bodyPitchDeg: tail->head line above the horizontal (nose up positive). wingElevationDeg: shoulder->wingTip from the rearward body axis, positive toward the back (dorsal): 0 = folded back along the body, +90 = straight up, beyond +/-90 = pointing forward, -90 = straight down (computed in a frame mirrored to face left, so the sign convention matches plate 755). Stroke top/bottom = frames where the near wing tip is highest/lowest relative to the tail tip. Period from tops and from silhouette repetition. Bob: eye height measured from the thick backdrop line (1190-1196 px in row 1, 1680-1686 px in row 2; the eye's height above it runs on smoothly from frame 6 to 7, so it is the same physical line), quadratic climb trend removed.
frameBoxesNote: Listed in time order, approximate to about 10 px. Frames 1-6 are row 1 and 7-12 row 2, numbered left to right.

timing.cyclesSource: muybridge-1887-catalogue (fraction of a cycle shown on the plate)
timing.observedComputed: the silhouette repeats exactly 6 frames later (1~7, 2~8, 3~9, 4~10, 5~11, 6~12) and the tops are at frames 6 and 12: 6 x 20 ms = 120 ms; +/-0.5 frame gives 7.7-9.1 Hz. The plate shows 11/6 = 1.8 cycles, not the catalogue's 1 1/2 (which would give 6.8 Hz).

frames.phase: early downstroke: near wing raised, tip up and behind the shoulder; far wing blurred above the head
frames.notes: Blur of the far wing shows it moving fast.

frames.phase: mid/late downstroke: near wing swept forward at about body level, tip ahead of the beak
frames.notes: Tail fanned; tail tip = rear edge of the fan.

frames.phase: bottom of stroke: near wing (lit underside) below and ahead of the shoulder
bottom / start of upstroke: wing below and ahead, tail spread
upstroke: near wing raised, tip up and behind the shoulder; far wing tip up beside the head
top of stroke: wing near vertical over the back
early downstroke: near wing up and behind, far wing blurred above; legs lowered
mid/late downstroke: near wing swept forward at body level
bottom of stroke: wing below and ahead of the shoulder
bottom / start of upstroke: wings low and forward, blurred
frames.notes: Head covered by the wing, so no body axis and no angles; tail tip at [2563,1607] and wing tip at about [2759,1589] noted only.

frames.phase: upstroke: near wing raised, tip up and behind
top of stroke: wing near vertical over the back
frames.notes: Wing tip close to the top of the frame's sky area.

downstrokeShare.computed: tip highest relative to the tail at frames 6 and 12 (203, 199 px), falling through 7 (137), 8 (42) to 9 (6), lowest at 3 (-21) / 4 (-3) in the first beat; frame 10 unmeasured. Top 6 -> bottom 9-10 = 3-4 intervals, bottom -> top 12 = 2-3 intervals of a 6-interval beat.

wingElevationDeg.computed: top = frames 6, 12; bottom/forward = frames 2, 3, 4, 8, 9; frames 1, 5, 7, 11 have the wing raised with the tip behind the shoulder. Frame 10 not measured.

derived.projectedSweepDeg: about 115-130 between the top (+94..+104) and the forward sweep (-136..-152, i.e. ahead of the shoulder and 30-45 deg below the forward body axis); the wing never goes straight down in side view
derived.climb: eye rises 206 px over 11 intervals relative to the backdrop line (11 px per interval at the start, 22 at the end); body pitch increases with it, from about 20 deg (frames 1-4) to 29-34 deg (frames 7, 8, 11, 12)

bodyBob.computed: after a quadratic trend the eye heights leave residuals within +/-5 px (frames 1-9, 11, 12), about 3% of the eye-to-tail length (about 157 px), with no pattern repeating at the 6-frame beat

findings: Wingbeat 8.3 Hz (silhouettes repeat every 6 frames at 20 ms = 120 ms). The catalogue fraction (1 1/2 cycles) undercounts: the plate shows 1.8 cycles. Plates 755, 756 and 757 together put pigeon flapping at 8.3-8.8 Hz.
A shallower climb than plates 755/756: body pitch starts at about 20 deg and rises to 34 deg as the climb steepens.

Here the downstroke is the longer half, about 55% (45-65%), unlike the steep climbs on plates 755 (42%) and 756 (30%). The stroke is also flatter in side view: the near wing goes from near vertical (+94..+104 deg) forward to just below the body line ahead of the shoulder (-136..-152 deg); it never points straight down, where it reached -111..-134 on plates 755/756.
Wing raised with the tip behind the shoulder (+65..+77 deg) both in late upstroke (frames 5, 11) and at the start of the downstroke (frames 1, 7, where the far wing is blurred above the head).
Legs: the feet hang below the body in frames 7, 8 and 11 (not measured).

Compared with figures/goose.json: goose flap/rush beat at 6/7 Hz with the wing swinging +26..+76 / +24..+82 deg from the rearward body axis and equal up and down time. This pigeon's top (+94..+104) is slightly above the goose top; its forward-down sweep to -136..-152 has no counterpart in the goose. The 55/45 down/up split here is close to Meir 2019's bar-headed goose (116/86 ms = 57%), which the goose motions do not show.
Not measured: frame 10 (head hidden); the 12 rear views (rows 3-4); the far wing; forward speed (each frame is a different camera).
